question: In which of the following years was the National Seeds Policy launched?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2002**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **National Seeds Policy** was launched in the year **2002** by the Government of India.
 
• The policy aimed at increasing the availability of **quality seeds** to farmers and boosting **agricultural productivity** in the country.
 
• It emphasized the development of a strong seed industry in India to make the country self-reliant in seed production and supply.
 
• The policy covered various aspects such as **seed production, certification, distribution, and quality control**.
 
• It also focused on promoting the use of **hybrid seeds** and ensuring the conservation of **genetic resources**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objectives of the National Seeds Policy, 2002:**

 
 
• To ensure the availability of **high-quality seeds** and planting materials for agriculture, horticulture, and forestry.
 
• To promote the development and use of **hybrid seeds** for enhancing crop productivity.
 
• To encourage the participation of the **private sector** in seed production and distribution.
 
• To strengthen the **seed testing and certification system** in the country.
 
• To establish an efficient system for **seed export and import** to meet the demands of the farming community.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Policy:**
 
 
• The policy helped in making India **self-sufficient** in seed production.
 
• It led to the development of a robust **seed industry** with both public and private sector involvement.
 
• Farmers gained access to **high-yielding and disease-resistant seed varieties**, contributing to increased agricultural productivity.
 
 
 
• **Seed Certification:**
 
 
• Seed certification was an essential aspect of the policy to ensure that farmers received **genuine and high-quality seeds**.
 
• The certification process involved rigorous testing for **purity, germination rate, and quality**.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Private Sector:**
 
 
• The policy encouraged private companies to invest in **seed research and development**.
 
• It facilitated collaboration between public and private sectors for the production and distribution of seeds.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Seed Replacement Rate (SRR):**

 
 
• The National Seeds Policy aimed to increase the **Seed Replacement Rate (SRR)**, which is the ratio of certified seeds used by farmers to the total seeds sown.
 
• A higher SRR ensures the use of **better-quality seeds**, leading to improved crop yields.
 
 
 
• **Conservation of Genetic Resources:**
 
 
• The policy emphasized the importance of conserving **genetic diversity** by maintaining a repository of indigenous and exotic germplasm.
 
• It also aimed to protect **farmers' rights** and traditional knowledge.
 
 
 
• **Role of ICAR:**
 
 
• The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (**ICAR**) played a significant role in the implementation of the policy.
 
• It provided technical support for seed research and facilitated the development of **new crop varieties**.
